title: Easy to miss
context: A 58-year-old smoker has had a fever, rigors and a cough with rusty sputum for four days. Crackles are hard to hear.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC / Dr Thomas Hooten
img.alt: Frontal chest X-ray with subtle hazy opacity in the right upper zone.

hints: Compare the two upper zones, rib space by rib space.
The haze sits above the level of the horizontal fissure, and the volume looks normal.
why: Subtle hazy airspace opacity in the right upper zone, with preserved lung volume and no mass: right upper lobe consolidation.
pearl: Collapse loses volume (the fissure and trachea pull up); pneumonia usually doesn't. In smokers and older adults, repeat the chest X-ray about 6 weeks after treatment to make sure an underlying tumour isn't hiding behind the consolidation.

title: Sudden breathlessness
context: A tall, thin 24-year-old developed sudden left-sided chest pain and breathlessness at rest.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Photographed by User Clinical Cases 00:42, 7 November 2006
img.alt: A large left-sided dark (lucent) area with no lung markings and a visible collapsed lung edge

hints: One side is much darker than the other, with no lung markings at the edge.
Look for a thin white line where the lung edge has pulled away from the chest wall.
why: A large left-sided dark (lucent) area with no lung markings and a visible collapsed lung edge: air in the pleural space.
pearl: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis (hypotension, distress, deviated trachea): decompress first, X-ray later. Small primary pneumothoraces in well patients can often be watched.

title: A fall on the shoulder
context: A 35-year-old fell while skiing. His shoulder looks squared off and he holds his arm away from his body.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Drfrancescsoler
img.alt: The humeral head lies below and in front of the glenoid instead of within it

hints: The ball of the humerus isn't sitting in its socket.
It has moved forwards and down, below the coracoid.
why: The humeral head lies below and in front of the glenoid instead of within it: anterior dislocation of the shoulder.
pearl: Check the axillary nerve (sensation over the 'regimental badge' area) before and after reduction. Posterior dislocations are easily missed: think seizures and electric shocks.

title: Fever that won't settle
context: An 82-year-old woman has had fevers, chills and weight loss for two weeks. She is on long-term steroids.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Benjamín Herreros, Isabel Plaza, Rebeca García, Marta Chichón, Carmen Guerrero and Emilio Pintor
img.alt: Countless tiny (1–3 mm) nodules evenly scattered through both lungs

hints: Zoom in: the lungs are full of tiny, evenly spread dots.
Each dot is about the size of a millet seed.
why: Countless tiny (1–3 mm) nodules evenly scattered through both lungs: a 'millet seed' pattern from blood-borne spread of TB.
pearl: The chest X-ray can be normal early in miliary TB. Look for TB elsewhere, including the meninges, and check HIV status.

title: A punch gone wrong
context: A 23-year-old has a swollen hand with a sunken knuckle after punching a wall.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Hellerhoff
img.alt: A fracture through the neck of the fifth metacarpal with the head tipped towards the palm

hints: Look at the little-finger side of the hand.
The bone is broken just behind the knuckle.
why: A fracture through the neck of the fifth metacarpal with the head tipped towards the palm: a boxer's fracture.
pearl: Any skin break over the knuckle after a punch is a human bite until proven otherwise: it needs washout and antibiotics.

title: A hugely swollen belly
context: A child with chronic constipation has severe abdominal distension and pain. Abdominal X-ray:
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Mont4nha
img.alt: A massively distended, inverted-U loop of large bowel rising out of the pelvis

hints: One enormously dilated loop fills much of the abdomen.
It arises from the pelvis and is shaped like a bean.
why: A massively distended, inverted-U loop of large bowel rising out of the pelvis: the 'coffee bean' sign of a twisted sigmoid colon.
assoc: High-fibre diets (common in Africa and Asia)
pearl: Sigmoid volvulus can often be untwisted with a flexible sigmoidoscope and rectal tube; recurrence is common, so surgery is usually planned afterwards.

title: Sore wrist after a fall
context: A 26-year-old has wrist pain after a fall. He is tender in the anatomical snuffbox.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.file: Scaphoid fracture - barely visible on initial X-ray.jpg
img.author: Mohamed Jarraya, Daichi Hayashi, Frank W. Roemer, Michel D. Crema, Luis Diaz, Jane Conlin, Monica D. Marra, Nabil Jomaah, and Ali Guermazi
img.alt: A faint lucent line across the waist of the scaphoid

hints: The fracture line is subtle. Look at the small bone at the base of the thumb.
Snuffbox tenderness points to this bone.
why: A faint lucent line across the waist of the scaphoid: a subtle scaphoid fracture.
pearl: Scaphoid fractures are often invisible on the first X-ray. If you suspect one, immobilise and arrange repeat imaging or MRI, because missed fractures can lead to avascular necrosis.
